skill.name: context7-efficient
skill.description: Fetches Context7 library documentation through local helper scripts, then filters the results into concise code examples, API signatures, and key notes.
skill.summary: Fetch Context7 documentation with token-efficient shell filtering.
skill.author: AbdullahMalik17

security_audit.summary: The skill is a legitimate Context7 documentation helper, but it relies on local shell scripts, subprocess execution, and network-backed MCP access. Most markdown backtick and library-resolution findings are false positives, while the real risks are unpinned npx execution, shell-based process management, and a Python stdio transport that uses shell=True.

remediation.issue: Unpinned npx execution of the Context7 MCP package.
remediation.suggestion: Pin @upstash/context7-mcp to a reviewed version or vendor a verified launcher, and document the expected package checksum or version.

remediation.issue: Python stdio transport starts command strings with shell=True.
remediation.suggestion: Replace shell=True with an argument array, or restrict --stdio to an allowlist of reviewed commands.

remediation.issue: PID files are stored under a predictable /tmp path and are trusted by start and stop helpers.
remediation.suggestion: Use a private runtime directory, validate PID ownership and command name before killing, and avoid broad pkill patterns.

remediation.issue: Shell scripts interpolate user values into JSON parameter strings.
remediation.suggestion: Build JSON parameters with jq, Python json.dumps, or another structured encoder to avoid malformed requests.

semantic_findings.title: Unpinned NPX Package Execution
semantic_findings.description: The scripts execute @upstash/context7-mcp through npx without a pinned version. A changed or compromised package release would run local code during documentation lookup.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited commands run npx -y @upstash/context7-mcp and do not specify a version. This is a clear supply-chain execution risk, although the package appears intended for the skill.

semantic_findings.title: Broad Process Termination Helper
semantic_findings.description: The stop script can force-kill the PID stored in a predictable temporary file and can use pkill with a pattern built from the port argument. This can terminate unintended local processes if the PID file or port value is unsafe.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The script reads /tmp/context7-mcp-${PORT}.pid, uses kill -9 on that PID, and falls back to pkill -f with the port value. The behavior is explicit process control, but impact is local.

content.value_statement: Library documentation can consume too many tokens during coding sessions. This skill fetches Context7 docs and filters them into concise examples, API signatures, and notes.
actual_capabilities: Resolves package names to Context7-compatible library identifiers.
Fetches library documentation through the Context7 MCP server.
Filters documentation into code examples, API signatures, and important notes.
Supports code and info modes for different documentation needs.
Supports pagination and direct library identifiers for deeper lookups.
Includes helper scripts for starting, stopping, and calling the MCP server.
limitations: Requires local shell access, Python, npx, and network access to Context7.
Depends on Context7 availability and the quality of upstream documentation.
Filtering may omit background context that appears in the full documentation.
Does not verify that returned examples are secure or current for every project.

use_cases.title: Look Up Framework Syntax
use_cases.description: Fetch concise examples for a specific framework feature during implementation.

use_cases.title: Compare API Usage Patterns
use_cases.description: Retrieve signatures and notes for a library before choosing an integration approach.

use_cases.title: Support Documentation Questions
use_cases.description: Answer library questions with focused Context7 excerpts instead of broad web searches.

prompt_templates.scenario: Faster lookup when the Context7 library ID is known.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use context7-efficient with the library ID /prisma/docs and topic queries.

prompt_templates.title: Research Multiple Pages
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced lookup across additional Context7 pages.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use context7-efficient to review page 1 and page 2 for React hooks, then summarize differences.

output_examples.output: A short response with selected hook examples, matching API signatures, and important usage notes.
A concise overview of setup steps, core concepts, and notes from Context7 documentation.

output_examples.input: Find Next.js routing documentation with a known library ID.
output_examples.output: Focused routing guidance with filtered examples and notes from the requested Context7 library.

best_practices: Use direct Context7 library identifiers when you already know the correct package.
Ask for a narrow topic to improve filtering quality and reduce missing context.
Review returned examples before applying them to production code.
anti_patterns: Do not use this skill as a general web search replacement.
Do not assume filtered excerpts include every warning from the full documentation.
Do not run the helper scripts in restricted environments without reviewing their command usage.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It fetches Context7 documentation and filters the result into shorter, coding-focused output.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it require internet access?
faq.answer: Yes. It uses Context7 through npx and MCP, so network access is required.

faq.question: Can it fetch full documentation?
faq.answer: It is designed for filtered excerpts, not full documentation archives.

faq.question: Why should users review it before installing?
faq.answer: The skill includes shell scripts, process control helpers, and unpinned npx package execution.

faq.question: What libraries are good fits?
faq.answer: It works best for libraries indexed by Context7, such as React, Next.js, Prisma, Express, and MongoDB.
